result.title: Intervene, Calibrate, Discover: Learning Causal Structure from Pixels
result.summary: Learning high-level causal variables from low-level observations is a central problem for artificial intelligence. With known node semantics but an unknown graph, visual readout errors can misalign model settings with environment intervention values. We address this mismatch by pairing image readouts with verified values attained through fixed round-robin interventions. With encoder and decoder frozen, a dimension-wise invertible calibration map puts visual responses and target settings in shared numerical units. After freezing this map, the agent selects interventions to resolve graph directions and fits local mechanisms to predict consequences; inverse calibration returns counterfactual states to the decoder's original coordinates. Across Domino, Pick-and-Place, Balance, Gears, CAUSAL3D, and CausalWorld, we evaluate graph discovery, intervention consequences, and counterfactual images. Controlled domino experiments show that interventions resolve orientation ambiguity left by equal additional observations. In a matched-data domino control, calibration reduces the mean error of predicted changes in other variables within the same factual context, relative to an uncalibrated model.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究节点语义已知但因果图未知时从像素学习高层因果变量：用固定轮转干预获得验证值，在冻结编码器与解码器的情况下学习逐维可逆校准映射，把视觉读出与干预设定对齐到同一数值单位，再据此选择干预以消解图方向并拟合局部机制，并反校准生成反事实图像。
AI.relevance_reason: 视觉读出与真实干预值错位、以及用校准把视觉响应统一到共享数值单位，可能为 LVR 中「视觉证据如何进入内部状态」与主动干预筛选证据提供可核查线索。
